raw_response:
I farm the way I always do: I start from last year, then I look at what the men around me are doing. My land is only 8 mu, not big, so every bag of fertilizer is money, but I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard because if yield drops, that hurts more than wasting a little. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed because the local good wheat seed has been steady here, and most people around me use it. I will put the main fertilizer down before sowing, then topdress once at jointing when the wheat starts taking off. With my well, I will give wheat 3 irrigations if the weather is normal: one after sowing if the ground is dry, one at jointing, one at grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like I did before, because hybrids fill the ear better and stand better if water is enough. Maize eats fertilizer hard, so I will not go light on nitrogen. I will split it, some at sowing and the rest before the big growth stage. I will watch weeds, armyworm, aphids, and rust like usual and spray when needed, not too many times, just enough to keep the crop clean. I will keep rotary tillage because it is what I know, it is quick, and on 8 mu it fits my money and labor.
